# Guarded documentation and development-dependency routing

This controller extends the existing automatic main-push public-feature route. It is not active until an independently reviewed bootstrap merge selects this immutable controller. No credentials, repository permissions or provider settings are added.

Classification reads actual Git objects before installing candidate dependencies. Each release is exactly one category. Public features retain their existing exact-tree review or narrow accepted-source-chain policy. Six reader documents permit only verified old-to-canonical URL prefix substitutions, preserving paths, prose and deployment guidance. Their main-push route waits for successful first-attempt ordinary CI and current exact-tree review, then records acceptance without building or deploying unchanged application bytes. Development dependencies require current exact-tree independent review, actual merge-parent association, unchanged production resolution graph/root scripts and metadata, and no changed install hooks. Runtime dependencies, arbitrary build scripts, authentication, billing, backend/private source and other controls remain rejected.

The dependency route authenticates current production against its guarded producer, controller, successful run and non-expired candidate/production-proof artifacts. It downloads those archives with bounded safe extraction and compares actual candidate output with the accepted producer: all non-worker runtime bytes must match; both service workers must independently satisfy the source template and asset/cache derivation. Changed runtime output is rejected, never automatically repinned. Expired or ambiguous evidence fails closed and needs a separately reviewed recovery; there is no silent baseline fallback.

Candidate tests/install/build run without release credentials and with install scripts disabled. A separate fresh runner compiles the same locked source without executing tests; every output byte, including the worker, must match the complete tested manifest. Precache names are sorted before hashing to make this full equality reproducible. Controller syntax analysis uses a separately pinned tool lock, not candidate packages. Before provider credentials are used, copied-public inventory is rebound to actual reviewed Git blobs. Provider steps re-read source/review, producer, production and intervening documentation continuity; artifacts cannot assert their own authority.

Preview byte/header checks and mandatory hosted behavior remain required. Promotion reuses the exact tested candidate, with same-run source/controller/tree/review bindings, serialization, current-main/production checks and explicit uncertain-outcome handling. A confirmed superseded source or changed baseline exits without upload. A failed or uncertain provider operation is not blindly retried. GitHub serialization does not provide atomic compare-and-swap against outside Cloudflare writers; production collisions remain an explicit failure boundary. Rollback is not automatic and requires preserved reviewed bytes plus fresh authorization and baseline verification.

Bootstrap is a narrow transition from the reconciled public source c15a0e08f0b85c04ba70c380042e794220cb3805: an independently reviewed immutable controller tree with only its zero workflow pin replaced by that controller's commit. It must merge with the expected actual parents, pass ordinary and release checks, and preserve current public behavior. The bootstrap cannot authorize its own review record.

These engineering gates do not prove business approval of text, package safety, real payment/authentication/storage acceptance, physical-device behavior or legal readiness. Existing denied authentication integration, direct production HTTP requests and archive sharing remain stopped. New sensitive operations retain their applicable separate approval requirements.
